notes: CHG-004 is RAISED and NOT APPROVED. These tests prove the code behaves as built; they do not resolve the requirement conflict with DATA-005, and no agent may.

Defect found and fixed inside this task: the client persona was first inserted mid-list in userSpecs, which renumbers every employeeCode after it. A top-up seed then handed the newcomer a code an existing employee already held and died on P2002 against EmployeeProfile.employeeNumber. Found only because prepare-test-db.mjs runs the seed WITHOUT --reset; the fresh path was green throughout and would have shipped it. Fixed by appending the persona last, which renumbers nobody, and verified by reset-then-top-up.

The 24 release-blocking failures were reconciled, not re-fixed: 20 are owned by SPEC-0004 (CONVERGED, R2) and 4 by SPEC-0005 (CONVERGED, R4). Both were already committed on dev/yourhan-next. The demo branch was based on f16ed67, which predates them. Resolved by merging a04c7e3 after removing 369 hand-copied corpus files that upstream now tracks; 364 were byte-identical to upstream and 5 were stale snapshots that upstream strictly supersedes. Nothing was reimplemented.

CONV-004 is closed by evidence, not by a workflow change: the suite passes at default file parallelism, which is exactly how CI invokes it. Two consecutive runs, 0 unexpected failures. The --no-file-parallelism requirement was an artefact of the pre-merge state.

The 2 skipped tests are observability.spec.ts's POSIX file-mode assertions, gated on process.platform !== 'win32'. They run on CI's Linux, so CI's skip-rejection gate does not fire. Not a suppression.

The E2E suite reads APP_URL from .env, which pins it to port 3005; the committed webServer gate therefore never matches a dev server started on 3000. Environmental, recorded rather than worked around: the run above used the project's own web-dev-3005 launch configuration and the committed config unmodified.
